evidence: src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:1213 defines `async def confirm_catalog(url: str, loaded: LoadedRuleSets) -> None`. The parameters are in the order (database URL, loaded rule sets). It returns early if state.confirmed is set. Otherwise it takes the lock and runs _check_catalog_blocking through run_blocking_sql. That calls check_catalog (1100-1172), which raises RuleSetCatalogError listing each mismatch (1170). A pass sets confirmed=True, so the check runs once until it passes. A failed check reruns on the next call (docstring 1217-1218). runner.py:228 calls `await confirm_catalog(cfg.database.url, loaded)`, which matches the signature. I did not check whether it is exported through a package `__all__`. `sqllens.rule_sets` is a module, and runner.py:219 imports the name from it directly.

select_rule_set(loaded: LoadedRuleSets, metadata: Mapping[str, Any]) (rule_sets.py:1008) takes any Mapping. It raises RuleSetRequestError with the REFUSED_* constants (rule_sets.py:858-868), all starting 'Request refused: '. RuleSetRequestError.__init__ passes the message to RuntimeError.__init__ (line 887), so str(exc) is that text. The runner (runner.py:213-224) builds a plain dict with only the three configured keys (rule_set, account_id, user_id) and calls select_rule_set(loaded, metadata). strip_reserved_metadata in query_database.py:657 removes reserved keys from request _meta, and the runner's dict has none, so nothing needs stripping. The runner catches RuleSetRequestError and uses str(exc) as detail (runner.py:225-226).

rule_sets.py:475-481 RuleSetFile has binding: Binding and metadata: MetadataKeys. MetadataKeys (90-95) has rule_set, account_id, user_id as Identifier (StrictStr pattern-constrained) key names. Binding.account_ids (81) is list[RuleSetId], RuleSetId a StrictStr, min_length=1, so indexable. LoadedRuleSets.file is RuleSetFile (used at 1016, 1027). runner.py:201-214 uses them accordingly.

CatalogConfirmation (rule_sets.py:715-720) is a non-frozen dataclass with `confirmed: bool = False`, so it is writable. runner.py:237 sets `loaded.catalog.confirmed = True` after `await confirm_catalog(...)` passes. confirm_catalog (rule_sets.py:1213-1229) returns early at 1221 when `state.confirmed` is true, and rechecks under the lock at 1224. ensure_catalog_confirmed (1232-1249) calls confirm_catalog, so per-case checks are skipped once the flag is set. confirm_catalog already sets the flag at 1229, so the runner's assignment is redundant. Setting True twice is idempotent and safe.

query_database.py:552-562 defines query_database_impl_with_widgets with keyword-only `metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None` and `agent: Agent | None = None`. runner.py:286-288 calls it with metadata=metadata, agent=verify_agent. _verification_metadata (runner.py:179-238) returns None when cfg.rule_sets.loaded is None (line 193) and otherwise a dict keyed by the file's [metadata] key names (line 214), which is the raw _meta mapping.

identity dict at runner.py:207-212 has keys rule_set, account_id, user_id, account_defaulted. VerificationIdentityError.__init__ (runner.py:131-141) keyword-only params are detail, missing, rule_set, account_id, user_id, account_defaulted. Every dict key matches a keyword param; no extras. The splat sites (226, 230, 232-236) pass kind positionally and detail explicitly, which don't collide with dict keys. So no TypeError from unexpected or duplicate keywords. The dict is a subset of the params (detail and missing are not in it), so 'exactly' holds for the four named identity params.

cli.py:645-651 builds `identity` only from options whose value `is not None` and calls run_verification(cfg, cases, **identity). The options default to None (cli.py:559-577), so no identity keywords are forwarded unless given. The stand-ins in tests/unit/test_cli_verify_memory.py are `_runner_call(cfg, cases, *, driver=None)` (line 72) and `capture(cfg, cases)` (line 423). Neither accepts rule_set, user_id or account_id, so they would raise TypeError if None values were forwarded. Omitting None keeps them working. An empty string is not None, so `--rule-set ''` and `--user ''` are forwarded. tests/unit/test_cli_rule_sets.py:249-251 and 264-274 pass such empty values and expect the exit-1 refusal that names the missing option.

rule_sets.py:1198-1210 _check_catalog_blocking opens its own pymysql connection with connect_timeout=5 (line 1191), read_timeout=write_timeout=30 (line 1195). check_catalog (1100-1172) reads information_schema TABLES and COLUMNS and, via _catalog_reads (1052-1097), checks every listed table, columns and predicate_columns, and unlisted owner_via/referenced_by link tables with their columns. Every compare column, parent_rule compare column (on parent_table) and owner_via link_user_column is type-checked against VALUE_TYPE_DATA_TYPES (1160-1168). Other rule-referenced columns on listed tables (is_null, inherit, referenced_by, link columns on listed tables) are required by the model validator (400-448) to be declared in columns/predicate_columns, so they are covered too. Absolute-claim input tried: a rule naming a link table not listed, or a parent_rule compare column. Both are traced and checked (1083-1094, 1076-1080). Repeat check: confirm_catalog (1213-1229) returns early when state.confirmed and sets it after a pass, so no later case repeats it.

Per-case: eval/runner.py:286 _prod_driver calls query_database_impl_with_widgets(forced, question, metadata=metadata, agent=verify_agent) for every case (loop at :299-300). With a rule-set file, that function (tools/query_database.py:651-695) writes logger.info('%s', audit_line(...)) in a finally block (:694), so every ending (served, refused, failed, cancelled) writes the line; this is the same code path as an MCP request. Adversarial input traced: a case that errors inside the agent or is refused by a guard still reaches the finally, so the per-case claim holds; metadata carries the identity so select_rule_set succeeds. No logging setup: grep of src/sqllens for basicConfig/dictConfig/addHandler/setLevel/RichHandler found nothing outside a vendored JS file; verify_memory (cli.py:541-665) configures none, so the root logger stays at the default WARNING level and the stdlib last-resort handler prints warnings to stderr while info is dropped. The docs sentence is in the context of a rule-set file (rule-sets.md:311 says no file means no lines), consistent with the code.

eval/runner.py:324 _extract_sql reads query_info['sql'] (runner.py:355-359). query_info is built in tools/_format.py:377,442-523 from the run_sql STATUS_CARD metadata['sql']. That card is created in agent/core/agent/agent.py:781-786 with metadata=tool_call.arguments, i.e. the model-written SQL, before the tool runs. Both guards rewrite via args.model_copy(update={'sql': rewritten}) (safety/rule_sets.py:894-895, safety/__init__.py:233), which makes a copy and does not mutate the original args or the card. Absolute-claim input tried: a rewriting guard in the run path (RLS or rule-set runner) with a row-rule filter. The rewritten SQL goes only to inner.run_sql and never reaches the card or query_info. So the compared SQL is pre-rewrite, and expected SQL needs no row-rule filter. The doc line at docs/external/rule-sets.md:258 matches the code.

rule_sets.py:1213-1229 confirm_catalog returns if state.confirmed, takes state.lock, rechecks confirmed, then awaits run_blocking_sql(_check_catalog_blocking, url, loaded) and sets state.confirmed = True only after it returns (a failure raises first). _check_catalog_blocking (1198-1210) uses connect timeout 5 (1191) and read/write timeout 30 (1195). ensure_catalog_confirmed (1232-1249) only calls confirm_catalog and maps exceptions, so it never runs the check itself. Absolute-claim trace: concurrent callers both entering after a pass hit the inside-lock recheck at 1224; grep over src finds no confirmed=False reset anywhere, so a pass is never undone. A failed check re-runs on the next call, but that is a failure, not a pass, and the claim only covers passes. Doc text is at rule-sets.md:60 (the item's line 152 is stale).

Agent loop (src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py:680-1141): each LLM response that is a tool call runs the tool, appends the result (success or error, 1035-1054) and calls the LLM again. The only early stop is consecutive 'Invalid arguments'/truncated failures (1056-1085, threshold 3), which a guard-refused run_sql with valid arguments does not trigger. So a refused run_sql (the unlisted-table case) still gets exactly one more model call, the even-numbered one, which returns 'done'. No retry path adds a third call: the only llm_service calls are send_request (1381) and stream_request (1460), each once per loop iteration. ScriptedLlm (test_row_rules_mysql.py:600-626) therefore consumes exactly one `pending` SQL per case. rule_sets.py:859-862 define the four refusal texts: no such rule set, account not bound, user ID invalid, rule set not confirmed. select_rule_set (1008-1038) runs the checks in this order: rule set name lookup (no such rule set), then account in binding.account_ids by exact decimal text (account not bound), then _user_id (user ID invalid), then not confirmed. Fixture (_rule_set_fixtures.py:54-73): account_ids ["5","6"], set "2" confirmed, set "3" unconfirmed, no set "9". Traced the cases at test_cli_rule_sets.py:280-286. (2,'05',7): '05' is not in ["5","6"], so account not bound. (2,'7',7): account not bound. (2,5,'0'): _user_id returns None because 0 is not > 0, so user ID invalid. (2,5,'-1'): fails the ^[0-9]+$ regex (rule_sets.py:62), so user ID invalid. (2,5,'abc'): same, user ID invalid. (3,5,7): account and user pass and the set is unconfirmed, so rule set not confirmed. (9,5,7): no such rule set. '007' is not in this parametrization. It is in the separate test at line 349. The code treats it as valid: it matches the regex and int('007') is 7, which is > 0. The wrapper text 'Request refused: ... (--rule-set ...)' is CLI formatting; the runner passes str(exc) through (runner.py:224-226).
